images.filename: Brackenhurst Campus, Nottingham Trent University - geograph.org.uk - 40843.jpg
images.caption: Brackenhurst Campus, Nottingham Trent University. The entrance to the Brackenhurst campus of Nottingham Trent University from the A612.  Brackenhurst is home to the School of Animal, Rural and Environmental Science.  The campus is located near Southwell, a market town, fourteen miles from Nottingham with regular public transport links into the city centre. It covers over 200 hectares of grounds, organised around a country house.

images.caption:
The Portland Building and East Drive I'd always assumed that this building was called this simply due to the fact that it was made of Portland stone (like its more photographed neighbour the Trent Building).
It maybe however, that it is named after the University's second Chancellor, The 7th Duke of Portland.

images.caption:
Former Unitarian Chapel Nottingham:
The chapel was opened in 1876, built to a design of the architect Stuart Colman, of Bristol. It was used as a place of worship for Unitarian Presbyterians in Nottingham until 1982. It was then converted into the Nottingham Lace Museum, but this venture proved financially unviable. The building was then converted to its current use, as a Pitcher and Piano public house.
